items.name: OpenAI GPT-6 rollout + Intelligent UI
items.summary: OpenAI rolled GPT-6 out to all ChatGPT tiers on October 7 (GPT-6 Sol for paid plans, GPT-6 Luna for Free/Go) alongside 'Intelligent UI', which lets the model answer with interactive charts, tappable buttons, forms and generated mini-tools instead of plain text. For ChatGPT's 1.2 billion weekly users, it is the biggest visible change to the interface since the product launched.

items.name: Anthropic Claude Haiku 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7 with API prices cut 90% for requests under 100,000 tokens ($0.10 input / $0.50 output per million), exactly matching OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna. It is Anthropic's fastest model yet, gains a one-million-token context window and an adjustable effort setting so developers can trade cost against intelligence.

items.name: Nous Research Hermes for Businesses
items.summary: Nous Research confirmed a $90M Series B at a $1.5B valuation on October 7 to commercialize its open-source Hermes agent framework, which has been cloned over 24 million times and now drives roughly 2.5% of global AI token usage. The raise funds 'Hermes for Businesses', a paid enterprise version with private deployment, SSO and audit for companies running customized agents.

items.name: Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk')
items.summary: Mistral AI launched its flagship Mistral Large 4 on October 6: a natively multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 1 trillion total parameters and 52B active per token, trained from scratch on 3,800 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in its own European data centers. It ships first as a public preview API with open weights promised by the end of October, pitched as Europe's answer to Chinese open-weight models like Kimi K3.

items.name: Reflection AI Beam
items.summary: The Nvidia-backed US startup unveiled Beam on October 5, its first open-weight model: a 501B-parameter MoE with only 23B active per token, which the company claims matches Z.ai's GLM-5.2 on reasoning at 3-4x less inference compute. Final red-teaming wraps this month, with weights, technical report and model card shipping under Apache 2.0 later in October.
